Apples at 1: one lot -> coins 44, stock [{6, days_left 5}]; a second lot -> [{12,5}], coins 38, row 'Apples: 1 a unit, stock 12'. Honey lot -> days_left null.

Fish at 6: one lot left 14 coins; the next Enter left coins and stock unchanged and showed 'Not enough coins', which was gone after the next word. With a 5000-coin slot, 16 apple lots -> 96 units; a 17th changed neither stock nor coins.

accept on day 1: order stays null. Day 2 orders (seeds 1-6), e.g. honey 4 for 54, apples 6 for 36: units in {4,6,8}, pay = units*ref*3//2, shown as 'Order: 4 Honey for 54'. accept -> taken true + 'Order taken: ...'; a second accept gave an identical state.
A later run on the same keep: title [Day Market, New season, Continue, Records, ...]; the slots row read 'Slot 1: Day 1 of 7, 50 coins'.

Saved a day-2 Morning (with stock, stall, raised price) under seed 1, then Continued it in a run with seed 77: day, coins, reputation, stock, stall, prices, upgrades, forecast, wholesale and order all equal. Enter on empty slot 2 stayed on slots.

Escape on Morning/Stall/Day -> texts [Paused, Resume, Title]. Resume and Escape restored states identical to before (tick aside). In the Day, 200 paused ticks left the clock at 5, same as without the pause. Title after buying a lot -> slot row still 'Slot 1: Day 1 of 7, 50 coins'.

next_good x0..6: apples, bread, cheese, fish, flowers, honey, apples; prev_good x1/x2: honey, flowers. Good/Price/Stock texts matched the selection each time.
put -> stall [{0,0,apples}], 'Crates: 1 of 8'; put on an occupied cell -> unchanged; take -> [], 'Crates: 0 of 8'; take on an empty cell -> unchanged; 9 puts -> 8 crates, 'Crates: 8 of 8'.

Stall [fish(2,1), bread(4,0)] and prices apples 6 / bread 5 were unchanged on the day-2 Morning, and again after Continue in a later run.

Seed 1 day 1: 70 visitors, ids 1..70, minutes strictly increasing within 0..479, all four types, wants distinct and numbering 2/1/2/3 by type. The same seed repeated the list, seed 2 changed it, and day 2's list differed and also repeated.

Clock went 0->1 at tick 20 (slow), 5 (fast), 1 (rush); 500 hold ticks left clock 0, tick 500, still day, 'Speed: Hold'. 10 slow ticks then fast: clock 1 after 3 more ticks (0 after 2). 61 rush ticks -> '09:01'.

On a busy setup, finish at tick 0 -> evening, clock 480, tick 0, taken 454, served 38, walked 2, passed 30. Identical (sales, coins, rep, stock, texts) to 480 rush ticks; 479 rush ticks is still in the day. finish at tick 5 gave the same result.

Per-minute rush traces of 4 busy days (seeds 1, 2, 3, 5): every visitor was on the aisle at x = clock - m for m..m+5 and off it from m+6. Traces used daymarket.run in process; spot-check equal to CLI output.

Same traces: every new basket item came from the front crate, or from the back crate only when the basket already held something; always a wanted good not already in the basket, at the type's units and the current price. No violations.
Apples at 4 in front col 2: all 12 apple-wanting cooks (seeds 1, 2) held 2 apples@4 with budget_left 32 at clock m+2. At price 5 no cook took apples; tourists took 1@6 at price 6 and none at 7.

Traces: empty-basket leavers were gone with passed +1 each minute; leavers with goods joined the queue with joined = arrival+6 (or went straight to a free till).

Traces: ends = start+2+goods; each sale at that minute paid the basket total (bargain less a tenth rounded down); coins/taken rose by the paid sum; stock fell from the fewest-days batch; served +1 per sale; reputation moved by +1 per sale.
Traces: no minute ended with a free till while the queue was non-empty. Visitors leaving the aisle to an empty queue with a free till were at a till that minute.

trace.how: context, new, read_again and how far the context grew are the run's own records. written_out a request is its growth less its answers (characters / 4), scaled to the run's exact total; of_which_unseen is that less the visible text (thinking). cost is what the request read and wrote, weighted; carried is what reading again what it added cost at every later request (start.carried: the same for what every request starts from). reading + writing is in_the_ledger
